claims.v: assess whether the specimen is of terrestrial origin and whether its bismuth could act as a terahertz waveguide

specimen could act as a terahertz waveguide.

claims.v: analysis does not indicate a non-terrestrial origin
claims.quote:
a modern and robust analysis of its chemical and structural composition and properties does not indicate that its
origin is non-terrestrial

claims.v: material never had the pure single-crystalline bismuth layer that could have acted as a terahertz waveguide
claims.quote:
nor do the data indicate that the material examined ever had the pure single-crystalline
bismuth layer that could possibly have acted as a terahertz waveguide

claims.v: material was manufactured terrestrially and then damaged by mechanical and heat stressors
claims.quote:
ORNL has a high level of confidence that all data indicate the material was
manufactured terrestrially-albeit using an uncommon mixture of elements by today's standards-and then incurred
damage caused by mechanical and heat stressors.

claims.quote:
Results align with previous DEVCOM
analyses, indicating that the structure and composition of the bismuth layers do not meet the requirements
necessary to serve as a terahertz waveguide.
